title: Stray Kids’ Latest Becomes Milestone 25th K-pop Album to Top Billboard 200: Full List
summary: BTS was the first K-pop act to top the all-genre chart; BLACKPINK was the first female K-pop act to do so.
body: Stray Kids’ This & That puts K-pop back in a familiar spot — No. 1 on the all-genre Billboard 200 chart. The EP is the 25th album or EP by a K-pop act to reach No. 1 on Billboard’s flagship albums chart in just over eight years. The first was BTS’ Love Yourself: Tear in June 2018. Stray Kids  has amassed nine No. 1 titles on the Billboard 200, which puts them out front among K-pop acts.  BTS is second, with seven No. 1 titles.  ATEEZ  is next in line with three No. 1s.  SuperM ,  BLACKPINK ,  TOMORROW X TOGETHER ,  NewJeans  and  TWICE  have all notched one No. 1 to date. In addition, one multi-artist K-pop soundtrack, KPop Demon Hunters , has reached No. 1. For all their success on the Billboard 200, Stray Kids have yet to crack the top 40 on the Billboard Hot 100. Their highest-charting single on that chart, “Chk Chk Boom,” debuted and peaked at No. 49 in August 2024. title: Noah Kahan Brings Out Chappell Roan for Surprise ‘California’ Performance at Rose Bowl Show
summary: The L.A. stadium concert marked Kahan’s biggest headlining performance to date.
body: Noah Kahan welcomed Chappell Roan for a surprise performance during his sold-out headlining show at Rose Bowl Stadium. The Pasadena, California, show on Saturday (Aug. 15) marked the singer-songwriter’s biggest headlining performance to date, drawing more than 56,000 fans to the famed venue as part of his The Great Divide World Tour. title: Bryan Adams Brings Out Pat Benatar & Neil Giraldo for Surprise Stevie Wonder Cover in Detroit
summary: Adams performed at Little Caesars Arena on Aug. 15.
body: Early during his concert Saturday night (Aug. 15) in Detroit, Bryan Adams spoke about having “the pleasure” of having Pat Benatar & Neil Giraldo supporting him on tour since last October, but noted that he’d “never had them on stage — before tonight.” And because, as Adams told the Little Caesars Arena crowd, “this is Motown city,” he invited the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame duo to join his band onstage for the first time, delivering a spirited rendition of Stevie Wonder ‘s “Superstition.” Adams and Benatar shared lead vocals, while Giraldo and Adams’ Keith Scott traded guitar licks. Afterwards, Adams said, “Thanks everybody. title: Never-Before-Released Photos of Madonna Released in Celebration of Her 68th Birthday: Shop the Prints
summary: Sonic Editions drops 17 high-quality prints of the "Material Girl."
body: All products and services featured are independently chosen by editors. However, Billboard may receive a commission on orders placed through its retail links, and the retailer may receive certain auditable data for accounting purposes. To celebrate her 68th birthday on Aug. 16, Madonna is getting 17 prints from limited-edition photography company Sonic Editions , with the collection spanning several decades of her legendary career. Most of the rare images of Madonna capture her early years in the 1980s, offering a look at the era that helped establish her as a pop culture icon. The selection includes candid moments, vintage photoshoots and an appearance alongside the late George Harrison. All prints come with either a black or white frame and include five size options with varying prices depending on the size. Shoppers can order the 11×14 inches at $189, 16×20 inches at $299, 20×24 inches at $399, 22×30 inches at $699 and 26×37 inches at $999. There is also the option to purchase the print-only copy, which starts at $99.
